name: Connecticut

teen.supervisedHours: 40 hours behind-the-wheel training plus 30 hours of classroom study for 16- and 17-year-olds (secondary sources)
teen.holdPermit: 120 days with commercial or high school driver education; 180 days with home training (secondary sources)
teen.nightLimit: Licensed 16 and 17: no driving 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. except work, school, religious activity or medical emergency (secondary). Permit: no curfew, but a qualified trainer must be in the car (DMV).
teen.passengerLimit: Permit: only the trainer, and parents or others with a licensed instructor (DMV). Licensed 16-17: first 6 months no passengers except instructor, parent/guardian or permit-period exceptions; second 6 months immediate family also (DPH).
teen.phone: Under 18: no cell phone or mobile electronic device at all, hands-free included (DMV). All drivers: no hand-held device; fines $200 / $375 / $625.

notes: Official DMV manuals page lists English and a Spanish PDF (revised 3/2023) plus a Spanish audio version; direct PDF URLs not confirmed, so the handbook fields point to the manuals page.

Knowledge test: commercial practice sites say 25 questions, 20 correct (80 percent) to pass; not confirmed on a DMV page, so exam fields are null. Whether the test is offered in Spanish was not found.
Permit trainer (non-professional): at least 20 years old, licensed four or more consecutive years, no suspension in those four years (DMV teen restrictions page).
Curfew, passenger, DUI, speeding over 20 mph, racing and reckless driving violations by 16-17-year-olds: license seized on the spot for 48 hours and car towed (DPH).

Move over (C.G.S. 14-283b): slow to a reasonable speed below the posted limit and, if in the adjacent lane, move over one lane unless unsafe. Sources disagree whether flashing lights are required; extended to more vehicles in 2017.
Right on red allowed after a full stop unless a sign forbids it (secondary).
School bus on divided highways: not confirmed from a reliable source; no question written.
Under 18 at the knowledge test: parent or guardian comes along or signs a consent form (secondary).
Research done with WebSearch only; official sites were unreachable from the sandbox (proxy 403).
